title.raw: 卷五十八 志第三十四 禮十二 Volume 58 Treatises 34: Rites 12

sentences.zh: 志第三十四 禮十二

translations.literal: Treatise 34, Rites 12
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 34: Rites, Part Twelve

sentences.zh: （凶禮一）〉

translations.literal: (Mourning Rites 1)
translations.idiomatic: (Mourning Rites, Part One)

sentences.zh: ○山陵

translations.literal: ○ Imperial Tombs
translations.idiomatic: ○ Imperial Tombs

sentences.zh: 次五曰凶禮。

translations.literal: The fifth category is called Mourning Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth category is mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 凡山陵、寢廟與喪葬、服紀及士庶喪制，皆以類編次。

translations.literal: All imperial tombs, ancestral temples, funerals and burials, mourning periods, and commoner mourning regulations are arranged in order by category.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial tombs, ancestral temples, funerals and burials, mourning periods, and commoner mourning regulations are all arranged here by category.

sentences.zh: 其謁陵、忌辰之禮，亦附載焉。

translations.literal: The rites for visiting tombs and anniversary observances are also appended herein.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for visiting tombs and observing death anniversaries are recorded here as well.

sentences.zh: ○山陵

translations.literal: ○ Imperial Tombs
translations.idiomatic: ○ Imperial Tombs

sentences.zh: 三十一年，太祖崩。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, Taizu passed away.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year of his reign, Taizu died.

sentences.zh: 禮部定議，京官聞喪次日，素服、烏紗帽、黑角帶，赴內府聽遺詔。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites fixed the regulations: on the day after capital officials heard the mourning news, in plain dress, black gauze caps, and black horn belts, they went to the inner palace to hear the final testament.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites laid down the rules: the day after capital officials received word of the death, they were to wear plain dress, black gauze caps, and black horn belts and go to the inner palace to hear the final testament.

sentences.zh: 於本署齋宿，朝晡詣几筵哭。

translations.literal: They fasted and lodged at their own offices, morning and evening going to the spirit table to weep.
translations.idiomatic: They kept vigil and lodged at their own offices, going morning and evening to weep before the spirit table.

sentences.zh: 越三日成服，朝晡哭臨，至葬乃止。

translations.literal: After three days they assumed full mourning dress, morning and evening attending the lying-in-state to weep, until the burial when it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After three days they put on full mourning, weeping morning and evening at the lying-in-state until the burial, when mourning attendance ended.

sentences.zh: 自成服日始，二十七日除。

translations.literal: From the day of assuming full mourning, they doffed it after twenty-seven days.
translations.idiomatic: From the day full mourning began, it was doffed after twenty-seven days.

sentences.zh: 命婦孝服，去首飾，由西華門入哭臨。

translations.literal: Ladies of rank wore mourning dress, removed head ornaments, and entered by the West Flowery Gate to weep at the lying-in-state.
translations.idiomatic: Ladies of rank wore mourning dress, removed their ornaments, and entered through the West Flowery Gate to weep at the lying-in-state.

sentences.zh: 諸王、世子、王妃、郡主、內使、宮人俱斬衰三年，二十七月除。

translations.literal: All princes, heir apparents, princess consorts, commandery princesses, inner eunuchs, and palace women alike wore the highest grade of mourning for three years, doffing it after twenty-seven months.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, heir apparents, princess consorts, commandery princesses, inner eunuchs, and palace women all wore the highest grade of mourning for three years, doffing it after twenty-seven months.

sentences.zh: 凡臨朝視事，素服、烏紗帽、黑角帶，退朝衰服。

translations.literal: Whenever they attended court and handled affairs, they wore plain dress, black gauze caps, and black horn belts; after court they wore full mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When attending court and conducting affairs, they wore plain dress, black gauze caps, and black horn belts; after court they changed into full mourning.

sentences.zh: 羣臣麻布員領衫麻布冠、麻絰、麻鞋。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers wore hemp round-collared shirts, hemp caps, hemp mourning bands, and hemp shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers wore hemp round-collared shirts, hemp caps, hemp mourning bands, and hemp shoes.

sentences.zh: 命婦麻布大袖長衫，麻布蓋頭。

translations.literal: Ladies of rank wore large-sleeved hemp long gowns and hemp head coverings.
translations.idiomatic: Ladies of rank wore large-sleeved hemp gowns and hemp veils.

sentences.zh: 明器如鹵簿。

translations.literal: Spirit objects were like an imperial guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit objects were arrayed like an imperial guard of honor.

sentences.zh: 神主用慄，制度依家禮。

translations.literal: Spirit tablets used chestnut wood; the regulations followed family rites.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit tablets were made of chestnut wood, following the regulations of family rites.

sentences.zh: 行人頒遺詔於天下。

translations.literal: Envoys promulgated the final testament throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys promulgated the final testament throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 在外百官，詔書到日，素服、烏紗帽、黑角帶，四拜。

translations.literal: Officials outside the capital, on the day the edict arrived, in plain dress, black gauze caps, and black horn belts, performed four bows.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in the provinces, on the day the edict arrived, wore plain dress, black gauze caps, and black horn belts and performed four bows.

sentences.zh: 聽宣讀訖，舉哀，再四拜。

translations.literal: After hearing the reading completed, they raised lamentation, then bowed four times again.
translations.idiomatic: After the reading was finished, they raised lamentation and bowed four times again.

sentences.zh: 三日成服，每旦設香案哭臨，三日除。

translations.literal: After three days they assumed full mourning; each morning they set up incense tables and wept at the lying-in-state; after three days they doffed mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After three days they put on full mourning; each morning they set up incense tables and wept at the lying-in-state; mourning was doffed after three days.

sentences.zh: 各遣官赴京致祭，祭物禮部備。

translations.literal: Each dispatched officials to the capital to offer sacrifice; sacrificial goods were prepared by the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Each province dispatched officials to the capital to offer sacrifice, with sacrificial goods prepared by the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 孝陵設神宮監並孝陵衛及祠祭署。

translations.literal: At Xiaoling were established the Spirit Palace Directorate, Xiaoling Guard, and Sacrificial Office.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaoling were established the Spirit Palace Directorate, the Xiaoling Guard, and the Sacrificial Office.

sentences.zh: 建文帝詔行三年喪，事在《本紀》。

translations.literal: The Jianwen Emperor issued an edict to observe three-year mourning; the matter is in the 《Basic Annals》.
translations.idiomatic: The Jianwen Emperor issued an edict mandating three-year mourning; the matter is recorded in the 《Basic Annals》.

sentences.zh: 以遭革除，喪葬之制皆不傳。

translations.literal: Because of the dynastic overthrow, the funeral and burial regulations were all not transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the dynastic overthrow, none of the funeral and burial regulations were preserved.

sentences.zh: 文帝崩於榆木川，遺詔一遵太祖遺制。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen passed away at Yumu River; his final testament wholly followed Taizu's final regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen died at Yumu River; his final testament followed Taizu's regulations in full.

sentences.zh: 京師聞訃，皇太子以下皆易服。

translations.literal: When the capital heard the mourning news, from the crown prince down all changed dress.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the capital, the crown prince and all below him changed into mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 宮中設几筵，朝夕哭奠。

translations.literal: Within the palace a spirit table was set up; morning and evening they wept and offered libation.
translations.idiomatic: A spirit table was set up in the palace, and mourners wept and offered libations morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 百官素服，朝夕哭臨思善門外。

translations.literal: All officials in plain dress, morning and evening wept at the lying-in-state outside the Gate of Reflecting on Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Officials wore plain dress and wept morning and evening at the lying-in-state outside the Gate of Reflecting on Goodness.

sentences.zh: 禮部定喪禮，宮中自皇太子以下及諸王、公主，成服日爲始，斬衰三年，二十七月除。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites fixed the mourning rites: within the palace, from the crown prince down and all princes and princesses, counting from the day of assuming full mourning, the highest grade of mourning for three years, doffed after twenty-seven months.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites fixed the mourning rites: within the palace, from the crown prince down through princes and princesses, full mourning began on the appointed day—the highest grade for three years, doffed after twenty-seven months.

sentences.zh: 服內停音樂、嫁娶、祭禮，止停百日。

translations.literal: During the mourning period music, marriage, and sacrifices were suspended, but only for one hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning, music, marriage, and sacrifices were suspended for one hundred days only.

sentences.zh: 文武官聞喪之明日，詣思善門外哭，五拜三叩頭，宿本署，不飲酒食肉。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials, on the day after hearing the mourning news, went outside the Gate of Reflecting on Goodness to weep, five bows and three kowtows, lodged at their offices, and did not drink wine or eat meat.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials, the day after receiving word of the death, went to weep outside the Gate of Reflecting on Goodness, performing five bows and three kowtows; they lodged at their offices and abstained from wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 四日衰服，朝夕哭臨三日，又朝臨十日。

translations.literal: On the fourth day full mourning dress; morning and evening weeping at the lying-in-state for three days, then morning attendance at the lying-in-state for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day they put on full mourning; for three days they wept morning and evening at the lying-in-state, then attended the lying-in-state each morning for ten days.

sentences.zh: 衰服二十七日。

translations.literal: Full mourning dress for twenty-seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Full mourning was worn for twenty-seven days.

sentences.zh: 凡入朝及視事，白布裹紗帽、垂帶、素服、腰絰、麻鞋。

translations.literal: Whenever entering court and handling affairs, white cloth wrapped gauze caps, hanging belts, plain dress, waist mourning bands, and hemp shoes.
translations.idiomatic: When entering court or conducting affairs, they wore white cloth–wrapped gauze caps, hanging belts, plain dress, waist mourning bands, and hemp shoes.

sentences.zh: 退朝衰服，二十七日外，素服、烏紗帽、黑角帶，二十七月而除。

translations.literal: After court full mourning dress; beyond twenty-seven days, plain dress, black gauze caps, and black horn belts; doffed after twenty-seven months.
translations.idiomatic: After court they wore full mourning; after twenty-seven days they wore plain dress, black gauze caps, and black horn belts, doffing mourning after twenty-seven months.

sentences.zh: 聽選辦事等官衰服，監生吏典僧道素服，赴順天府，朝夕哭臨三日，又朝臨十日。

translations.literal: Awaiting-selection and handling-affairs officials wore full mourning; supervising students, clerks, monks, and Daoists plain dress; they went to Shuntian Prefecture, morning and evening weeping at the lying-in-state for three days, then morning attendance for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Officials awaiting selection and those handling affairs wore full mourning; supervising students, clerks, monks, and Daoist priests wore plain dress and went to Shuntian Prefecture to weep morning and evening at the lying-in-state for three days, then attend each morning for ten days.

sentences.zh: 命婦第四日由西華門入，哭臨三日，俱素服，二十七日除。

translations.literal: Ladies of rank on the fourth day entered by the West Flowery Gate, wept at the lying-in-state for three days, all in plain dress, doffed after twenty-seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Ladies of rank entered through the West Flowery Gate on the fourth day and wept at the lying-in-state for three days, all in plain dress; mourning was doffed after twenty-seven days.

sentences.zh: 凡音樂祭祀，並輟百日。

translations.literal: All music and sacrifices were likewise suspended for one hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Music and sacrifices were likewise suspended for one hundred days.

sentences.zh: 婚嫁，官停百日，軍民停一月。

translations.literal: Marriage: officials suspended for one hundred days, soldiers and commoners for one month.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage was suspended for one hundred days among officials and one month among soldiers and commoners.

sentences.zh: 軍民素服，婦人素服不妝飾，俱二十七日。

translations.literal: Soldiers and commoners in plain dress; women in plain dress without adornment, all for twenty-seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and commoners wore plain dress; women wore plain dress without adornment, all for twenty-seven days.

sentences.zh: 在外以聞喪日爲始，越三日成服，就本署哭臨，餘如京官。

translations.literal: Outside the capital, counting from the day of hearing mourning news, after three days assuming full mourning, at their own offices weeping at the lying-in-state; the rest as capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces, counting from the day word arrived, full mourning began after three days; officials wept at the lying-in-state at their own offices, with the rest following capital practice.

sentences.zh: 命婦素服舉哀三日，二十七日除。

translations.literal: Ladies of rank in plain dress raised lamentation for three days, doffed after twenty-seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Ladies of rank in plain dress raised lamentation for three days and doffed mourning after twenty-seven days.

sentences.zh: 軍民男女皆素服十三日，餘俱如京師。

translations.literal: Soldiers and commoners, men and women, all in plain dress for thirteen days; the rest all as in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and commoners of both sexes wore plain dress for thirteen days; all other rules followed those of the capital.

sentences.zh: 凡京官服，給麻布一匹自制。

translations.literal: For all capital officials' dress, one bolt of hemp cloth was issued for self-making.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials were issued one bolt of hemp cloth each to make their own mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 四夷使臣，工部造與。

translations.literal: For the four barbarians' envoys, the Ministry of Works manufactured and gave them.
translations.idiomatic: For foreign envoys, the Ministry of Works manufactured and supplied mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 諸王公主遣官及內外文武官詣几筵祭祀者，光祿寺備物，翰林院撰文，禮部引赴思善門外行禮。

translations.literal: When princes and princesses dispatched officials and inner and outer civil and military officials went to the spirit table to sacrifice, the Court of Imperial Entertainments prepared the goods, the Hanlin Academy composed the text, and the Ministry of Rites led them to perform rites outside the Gate of Reflecting on Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: When princes and princesses dispatched officials and civil and military officials within and without the palace came to sacrifice at the spirit table, the Court of Imperial Entertainments prepared the offerings, the Hanlin Academy composed the text, and the Ministry of Rites led them to perform rites outside the Gate of Reflecting on Goodness.

sentences.zh: 京城聞喪日爲始，寺觀各鳴鐘三萬杵，禁屠宰四十九日。

translations.literal: Counting from the day the capital heard mourning news, each temple and monastery struck the bell thirty thousand strokes, and slaughter was forbidden for forty-nine days.
translations.idiomatic: From the day the capital received word of the death, every temple and monastery struck its bell thirty thousand times, and slaughter was forbidden for forty-nine days.

sentences.zh: 喪將至，文武官衰服，軍民素服赴居庸關哭迎。

translations.literal: When the bier was about to arrive, civil and military officials in full mourning dress, soldiers and commoners in plain dress, went to Juyong Pass to weep and welcome it.
translations.idiomatic: As the bier approached, civil and military officials in full mourning and soldiers and commoners in plain dress went to Juyong Pass to weep and welcome it.

sentences.zh: 皇太子、親王及羣臣皆衰服哭迎於郊。

translations.literal: The crown prince, imperial princes, and the assembled ministers all in full mourning dress wept and welcomed it in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, imperial princes, and ministers all wore full mourning and wept to welcome the bier in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 至大內，奉安於仁智殿，加斂，奉納梓宮。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the inner palace, it was reverently placed in the Hall of Benevolence and Wisdom, additional encoffining was performed, and it was reverently placed in the catalpa coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the inner palace, the remains were reverently placed in the Hall of Benevolence and Wisdom, further encoffined, and laid in the imperial bier.

sentences.zh: 遣中官奉大行皇帝遺衣冠。

translations.literal: Palace eunuchs were dispatched to present the late emperor's surviving robes and cap.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs were dispatched to present the late emperor's surviving robes and cap.

sentences.zh: 作書賜漢王、趙王。

translations.literal: Letters were composed and bestowed on the Prince of Han and the Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Letters were composed and sent to the Prince of Han and the Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 禮臣言：「喪服已逾二十七日，請如遺命，以日易月。

translations.literal: Rites officials said: "Mourning dress has already exceeded twenty-seven days; we request, as the final testament commands, to substitute days for months."
translations.idiomatic: Rites officials said: "Mourning dress has already been worn for more than twenty-seven days; we ask, as the final testament commands, to count days in place of months."

sentences.zh: 」帝以梓宮在殯，不忍易，素冠、麻衣、麻絰視朝，退仍衰服，羣臣聽其便。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the catalpa coffin was in lying-in-state, could not bear to change; in plain caps, hemp garments, and hemp mourning bands he attended court; after court he still wore full mourning; the assembled ministers were left to their convenience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, with the imperial bier still in lying-in-state, could not bring himself to change; he attended court in a plain cap, hemp garments, and hemp mourning bands, then resumed full mourning after court, while ministers were left to do as they saw fit.

sentences.zh: 十二月，禮部進葬祭儀：發引前三日，百官齋戒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Ministry of Rites presented the burial and sacrifice rites: three days before the procession departed, all officials fasted and purified themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, the Ministry of Rites presented the burial and sacrifice rites: three days before the funeral procession departed, all officials observed purification.

sentences.zh: 遣官以葬期告天地宗社，皇帝衰服告几筵，皇太子以下皆衰服隨班行禮。

translations.literal: Officials were dispatched to announce the burial date to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral altars; the emperor in full mourning announced to the spirit table; from the crown prince down all in full mourning followed in rank to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were dispatched to announce the burial date to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral altars; the emperor in full mourning announced to the spirit table; the crown prince and all below wore full mourning and followed in rank to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 百官衰服朝一臨，至發引止。

translations.literal: All officials in full mourning attended court once each to attend the lying-in-state, until the procession departed when it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in full mourning attended the lying-in-state once each day at court until the procession departed, when attendance ceased.

sentences.zh: 前一日，遣官祭金水橋、午門、端門、承天門、大明門、德勝門並所過河橋、京都應祀神祇及經過應祀神祠，儀用酒果餚饌。

translations.literal: On the previous day, officials were dispatched to sacrifice at the Golden Water Bridge, Meridian Gate, Upright Gate, Gate of Receiving Heaven, Great Bright Gate, Victorious Virtue Gate, and all river bridges passed along the way, the spirits of the capital due for sacrifice, and spirit shrines passed that were due for sacrifice; the rites used wine, fruit, and prepared foods.
translations.idiomatic: On the previous day, officials were dispatched to sacrifice at the Golden Water Bridge, Meridian Gate, Upright Gate, Gate of Receiving Heaven, Great Bright Gate, Victorious Virtue Gate, every river bridge along the route, the spirits of the capital due for sacrifice, and every shrine along the way that required offerings, using wine, fruit, and prepared foods.

sentences.zh: 是夕，設辭奠，帝后太子以下皆衰服，以序致祭。

translations.literal: That evening, a farewell offering was set up; the emperor, empress, crown prince, and all below in full mourning, in order offered sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: That evening a farewell offering was set up; the emperor, empress, crown prince, and all below wore full mourning and offered sacrifice in order of rank.

sentences.zh: 司禮監、禮部、錦衣衛命執事者設大昇轝、陳葬儀於午門外並大明門外。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Ceremonial, Ministry of Rites, and Embroidered-Uniform Guard ordered the officiants to set up the great lifting carriage and display the burial rites outside the Meridian Gate and outside the Great Bright Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Ceremonial, Ministry of Rites, and Embroidered-Uniform Guard ordered officiants to set up the great lifting carriage and display the burial regalia outside the Meridian Gate and the Great Bright Gate.

sentences.zh: 將發，設啓奠。

translations.literal: When about to depart, a departure offering was set up.
translations.idiomatic: Just before departure, a departure offering was set up.

sentences.zh: 皇帝暨皇太子以下衰服四拜。

translations.literal: The emperor together with the crown prince and all below in full mourning performed four bows.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, crown prince, and all below in full mourning performed four bows.

sentences.zh: 奠帛、獻酒、讀祝，四拜。

translations.literal: They offered silks, presented wine, read the prayer, and bowed four times.
translations.idiomatic: They offered silks, presented wine, read the prayer, and bowed four times.

sentences.zh: 舉哀，興，哀止，望瘞。

translations.literal: They raised lamentation, rose, lamentation ceased, and gazed toward the burial.
translations.idiomatic: They raised lamentation, rose, ceased lamentation, and gazed toward the burial site.

sentences.zh: 執事者升，徹帷幙，拂拭梓宮，進龍輴於几筵殿下。

translations.literal: The officiants ascended, removed the curtains, dusted the catalpa coffin, and advanced the dragon hearse before the spirit table hall.
translations.idiomatic: Officiants ascended, removed the curtains, dusted the imperial bier, and brought the dragon hearse before the spirit table hall.

sentences.zh: 設神亭、神帛輿、諡冊寶輿于丹陛上，設祖奠如啓奠儀。

translations.literal: Spirit pavilions, spirit-silk carriages, and posthumous-title book and seal carriages were set on the red steps; an ancestral offering was set up with rites like the departure offering.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit pavilions, spirit-silk carriages, and carriages for the posthumous-title book and seals were set on the red steps; an ancestral offering was set up following the same rites as the departure offering.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣梓宮前，西向立。

translations.literal: The emperor went before the catalpa coffin and stood facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went before the imperial bier and stood facing west.

sentences.zh: 皇太子、親王以次侍立。

translations.literal: The crown prince and imperial princes in order stood attending.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and imperial princes stood in attendance in order of rank.

sentences.zh: 內侍於梓宮前奏，請靈駕進發，捧冊寶、神帛置輿中；

translations.literal: Inner attendants before the catalpa coffin announced, requesting the spirit carriage to advance; they bore the book and seal, spirit silks, and placed them in the carriages;
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants announced before the imperial bier, requesting the spirit carriage to advance; they bore the book and seals and spirit silks and placed them in the carriages;

sentences.zh: 次銘旌出；

translations.literal: next the name banner came out;
translations.idiomatic: next the name banner was brought out;

sentences.zh: 執事官升梓宮，內執事持翣左右蔽。

translations.literal: officiating officials raised the catalpa coffin; inner officiants held feather fans left and right to screen it.
translations.idiomatic: officiating officials raised the imperial bier while inner attendants held feather fans on either side to screen it.

sentences.zh: 降殿，內侍官請梓宮升龍輴，執事官以彩帷幕梓宮，內侍持傘扇侍衛如儀。

translations.literal: Descending the hall, inner attendants requested the catalpa coffin to ascend the dragon hearse; officiating officials draped the catalpa coffin with colored curtains; inner attendants held umbrellas and fans attending as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: As they descended the hall, inner attendants requested that the imperial bier be placed on the dragon hearse; officiants draped it with colored curtains while inner attendants held umbrellas and fans in attendance as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 舊御儀仗居前，冊寶、神帛、神亭、銘旌以次行。

translations.literal: The former imperial guard of honor went before; the book and seal, spirit silks, spirit pavilion, and name banner proceeded in order.
translations.idiomatic: The former imperial guard of honor went first; the book and seals, spirit silks, spirit pavilion, and name banner followed in order.

sentences.zh: 皇帝由殿左門出，后妃、皇太子、親王及宮妃後隨。

translations.literal: The emperor exited by the hall's left gate; empresses, the crown prince, imperial princes, and palace consorts followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exited through the hall's left gate, followed by empresses, the crown prince, imperial princes, and palace consorts.

sentences.zh: 至午門內，設遣奠，如祖奠儀。

translations.literal: Upon reaching inside the Meridian Gate, a dispatch offering was set up, with rites like the ancestral offering.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the Meridian Gate a dispatch offering was set up, following the same rites as the ancestral offering.

sentences.zh: 內侍請靈駕進發，皇帝以下哭盡哀，俱還宮。

translations.literal: Inner attendants requested the spirit carriage to advance; from the emperor down they wept to the full extent of grief, then all returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants requested the spirit carriage to advance; the emperor and all below wept their fill, then all returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 梓宮至午門外，禮官請梓宮升大升轝。

translations.literal: When the catalpa coffin reached outside the Meridian Gate, rites officials requested the catalpa coffin to ascend the great lifting carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial bier reached outside the Meridian Gate, rites officials requested that it be placed on the great lifting carriage.

sentences.zh: 執事官奉升轝訖，禮官請靈駕進發。

translations.literal: Officiating officials reverently completed raising it to the carriage; rites officials requested the spirit carriage to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Officiants finished placing the bier on the carriage; rites officials requested the spirit carriage to advance.

sentences.zh: 皇太子、親王以下哭送出端門外，行辭祖禮。

translations.literal: The crown prince, imperial princes, and all below weeping escorted it outside the Upright Gate and performed the rite of bidding farewell to the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, imperial princes, and all below escorted the bier weeping to outside the Upright Gate and performed the rite of bidding farewell to the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 執事官設褥位於太廟帛香案前。

translations.literal: Officiating officials set a cushion position before the Grand Temple's silk incense table.
translations.idiomatic: Officiants set a cushion before the silk incense table in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 皇太子易常服，捧神帛，由左門入，至褥位跪，置神帛於褥，興，正立於神後跪。

translations.literal: The crown prince changed to regular dress, bore the spirit silks, entered by the left gate, reached the cushion position and knelt, placed the spirit silks on the cushion, rose, and correctly stood kneeling behind the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince changed into regular dress, bore the spirit silks, entered through the left gate, knelt at the cushion, placed the spirit silks upon it, rose, and knelt upright behind the spirit.

sentences.zh: 禮官跪於左，奏太宗體天弘道高明廣運聖武神功純仁至孝文皇帝謁辭。

translations.literal: A rites official knelt on the left and announced: "Taizong, the Emperor who embodies Heaven, expands the Way, is lofty and bright, broadly carries fortune, sage in martial affairs and divine in accomplishment, purely benevolent and supremely filial, Cultured Emperor, pays his farewell visit."
translations.idiomatic: A rites official knelt on the left and announced: "Taizong, Emperor who embodies Heaven, expands the Way, is lofty and bright, broadly carries fortune, sage in war and divine in accomplishment, purely benevolent and supremely filial, Cultured Emperor, pays his farewell visit."

sentences.zh: 皇太子俯伏，興。

translations.literal: The crown prince prostrated himself, then rose.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince prostrated himself, then rose.

sentences.zh: 贊五拜三叩頭畢，皇太子捧神帛興，以授禮官。

translations.literal: The usher completed five bows and three kowtows; the crown prince bore the spirit silks, rose, and handed them to the rites official.
translations.idiomatic: After five bows and three kowtows were completed, the crown prince bore the spirit silks, rose, and handed them to the rites official.

sentences.zh: 禮官安輿中，請靈駕進發。

translations.literal: The rites official placed them in the carriage and requested the spirit carriage to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The rites official placed them in the carriage and requested the spirit carriage to advance.

sentences.zh: 皇太子仍喪服，親王以下隨行。

translations.literal: The crown prince again wore mourning dress; imperial princes and all below followed along.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince again put on mourning dress; imperial princes and all below followed along.

sentences.zh: 梓宮由大明中門出，皇太子以下由左門出，步送至德勝門外，乘馬至陵，在途朝夕哭奠臨。

translations.literal: The catalpa coffin exited by the Great Bright central gate; the crown prince and all below exited by the left gate, escorting on foot to outside the Victorious Virtue Gate, then mounting horses to the tomb; along the way morning and evening weeping, libation, and attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial bier exited through the Great Bright central gate; the crown prince and all below left through the left gate and escorted it on foot to outside the Victorious Virtue Gate, then mounted horses for the tomb, weeping and offering libations morning and evening along the way.

sentences.zh: 諸王以下及百官、軍民耆老、四品以上命婦，以序沿途設祭。

translations.literal: From princes down, all officials, aged soldiers and commoners, and ladies of rank of the fourth grade and above, in order set up offerings along the route.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, officials, aged soldiers and commoners, and ladies of rank of the fourth grade and above set up offerings along the route in order of rank.

sentences.zh: 文武官不繫山陵執事者悉還。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials not attached to tomb officiating duties all returned.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials not assigned to tomb duties all returned.

sentences.zh: 至陵，執事官先陳龍輴於獻殿門外，俟大升轝至。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the tomb, officiating officials first displayed the dragon hearse outside the Offering Hall gate, awaiting the great lifting carriage's arrival.
translations.idiomatic: At the tomb, officiants first displayed the dragon hearse outside the Offering Hall gate, awaiting the great lifting carriage.

sentences.zh: 禮官請靈駕降轝，升龍輴詣獻殿。

translations.literal: Rites officials requested the spirit carriage to descend from the carriage and ascend the dragon hearse to proceed to the Offering Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Rites officials requested that the spirit carriage be lowered and the bier placed on the dragon hearse to proceed to the Offering Hall.

sentences.zh: 執事官奉梓宮入，皇太子、親王由左門入，安奉訖，行安神禮。

translations.literal: Officiating officials reverently brought the catalpa coffin in; the crown prince and imperial princes entered by the left gate; when placement was completed, they performed the rite of settling the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Officiants reverently brought the imperial bier inside; the crown prince and imperial princes entered through the left gate; once placement was complete, they performed the rite of settling the spirit.

sentences.zh: 皇太子四拜，興，奠酒，讀祝。

translations.literal: The crown prince bowed four times, rose, offered wine, and read the prayer.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince bowed four times, rose, offered wine, and read the prayer.

sentences.zh: 俯伏，興，四拜，舉哀。

translations.literal: He prostrated himself, rose, bowed four times, and raised lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself, rose, bowed four times, and raised lamentation.

sentences.zh: 親王以下陪拜，如常儀。

translations.literal: Imperial princes and all below accompanied in bowing, as in the regular rites.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes and all below accompanied him in bowing, following the usual rites.

sentences.zh: 遣官祀告后土並天壽山，設遷奠禮，如上儀。

translations.literal: Officials were dispatched to sacrifice and announce to the Earth Queen and Mount Heavenly Longevity; a relocation offering was set up, with rites as above.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were dispatched to sacrifice and announce to the Earth Queen and Mount Heavenly Longevity; a relocation offering was set up following the same rites as above.

sentences.zh: 將掩玄宮，皇太子以下詣梓宮前跪。

translations.literal: When about to seal the dark chamber, from the crown prince down they proceeded to kneel before the catalpa coffin.
translations.idiomatic: When the underground palace was about to be sealed, the crown prince and all below him proceeded to kneel before the imperial bier.

sentences.zh: 內侍請靈駕赴玄宮，執事官奉梓宮入皇堂。

translations.literal: Palace attendants requested the spirit carriage proceed to the dark chamber; officiating officials reverently bore the catalpa coffin into the imperial hall.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants requested that the spirit carriage proceed to the underground palace, and officiants reverently carried the imperial bier into the imperial hall.

sentences.zh: 內侍捧冊寶置於前，陳明器，行贈禮。

translations.literal: Palace attendants bore the registers and seals and placed them before; bright objects were displayed; the gift-offering rite was performed.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants brought forward the registers and seals and set them in place, displayed the grave goods, and performed the gift-offering rite.

sentences.zh: 皇太子四拜興，奠酒，進贈。

translations.literal: The crown prince bowed four times and rose, offered wine, and presented the gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince bowed four times, rose, offered wine, and presented the burial gifts.

sentences.zh: 執事官捧玉帛進於右，皇太子受獻，以授內執事，捧入皇堂安置。

translations.literal: Officiating officials bore jade and silks forward on the right; the crown prince received the offering and handed it to inner attendants, who bore it into the imperial hall and placed it.
translations.idiomatic: Officiants brought jade and silks forward on the right; the crown prince received the offering and passed it to inner attendants, who carried it into the imperial hall and set it in place.

sentences.zh: 俯伏，興，四拜，舉哀，遂掩玄宮。

translations.literal: He prostrated himself, rose, bowed four times, raised lamentation, and then sealed the dark chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself, rose, bowed four times, raised lamentation, and then sealed the underground palace.

sentences.zh: 行饗禮，如遷奠儀。

translations.literal: The feasting rite was performed as in the relocation offering ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The feasting rite was performed following the same procedure as the relocation offering.

sentences.zh: 遣官祀謝后土及天壽山。

translations.literal: Officials were dispatched to sacrifice in thanks to the Earth Queen and Mount Heavenly Longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices of thanks to the Earth Queen and Mount Heavenly Longevity.

sentences.zh: 設香案玄宮門外，設題主案於前，西向。

translations.literal: An incense table was set outside the dark chamber gate; a spirit-tablet inscription table was set before, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: An incense table was set outside the underground palace gate, and a tablet-inscription table was placed before it, facing west.

sentences.zh: 設皇太子拜位於前，北向。

translations.literal: The crown prince's bowing position was set before, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's place for bowing was set before it, facing north.

sentences.zh: 內侍盥手奉主置案上，題主官盥手西向題畢，內侍奉主安於神座，藏帛箱中。

translations.literal: Palace attendants washed hands, bore the tablet and placed it on the table; the tablet inscription official washed hands, faced west and completed the inscription; palace attendants placed the tablet on the spirit seat and stored silks in the chest.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants washed their hands, brought the tablet forward, and placed it on the table; the tablet-inscription official washed his hands, faced west, and completed the inscription; attendants then installed the tablet on the spirit seat and stored the silks in a chest.

sentences.zh: 內侍奏請太宗文皇帝神靈上神主。

translations.literal: Palace attendants announced a request that the spirit of Taizong, Cultured Emperor, ascend to the spirit tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants announced a request that the spirit of Taizong, the Cultured Emperor, ascend to the spirit tablet.

sentences.zh: 贊四拜，興，獻酒，讀祝。

translations.literal: The usher called for four bows; they rose, offered wine, and read the prayer.
translations.idiomatic: The usher called for four bows; the mourners rose, offered wine, and read the prayer.

sentences.zh: 俯伏，興，四拜，舉哀。

translations.literal: He prostrated himself, rose, bowed four times, and raised lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself, rose, bowed four times, and lamented.

sentences.zh: 內侍啓櫝受主訖，請神主降座升輿。

translations.literal: Palace attendants opened the case and received the tablet; when done, they requested the spirit tablet descend from the seat and ascend the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants opened the case and received the tablet; when this was done, they requested that the spirit tablet descend from its seat and be placed on the carriage.

sentences.zh: 至獻殿，奏請神主降輿升座，行初虞禮。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the Offering Hall, they announced a request that the spirit tablet descend from the carriage and ascend the seat; the first comforting sacrifice was performed.
translations.idiomatic: At the Offering Hall, they announced a request that the spirit tablet be lowered from the carriage and installed on its seat, and the first comforting sacrifice was performed.

sentences.zh: 皇太子四拜，初獻，奠帛酒，讀祝，俯伏，興。

translations.literal: The crown prince bowed four times, made the first offering, presented silks and wine, read the prayer, prostrated himself, and rose.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince bowed four times, made the first offering, presented silks and wine, read the prayer, then prostrated himself and rose.

sentences.zh: 亞獻、終獻，四拜，舉哀，望瘞。

translations.literal: The second and final offerings were made; they bowed four times, raised lamentation, and gazed toward the burial.
translations.idiomatic: The second and final offerings were made; they bowed four times, raised lamentation, and gazed toward the burial place.

sentences.zh: 內官捧神帛箱埋於殿前，焚兇器於野。

translations.literal: Inner officials bore the spirit silk chest and buried it before the hall; unlucky objects were burned in the wild.
translations.idiomatic: Inner officials buried the chest of spirit silks before the hall and burned the unlucky objects in the open country.

sentences.zh: 葬日初虞，柔日再虞，剛日三虞，後間日一虞，至九虞止。

translations.literal: On the burial day the first comforting sacrifice; on a yin day the second; on a yang day the third; thereafter one every alternate day, until the ninth and then it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The first comforting sacrifice was held on the burial day, the second on a yin day, the third on a yang day, and thereafter one every other day until the ninth, when the rites ceased.

sentences.zh: 在途，皇太子行禮。

translations.literal: Along the way, the crown prince performed the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Along the route, the crown prince performed the rites.

sentences.zh: 還京，皇帝行禮。

translations.literal: Upon returning to the capital, the emperor performed the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned to the capital, the emperor performed the rites.

sentences.zh: 神主將還，內侍請神主降座升輿，儀仗侍衛如儀。

translations.literal: When the spirit tablet was about to return, palace attendants requested it descend from the seat and ascend the carriage; guard of honor and escort as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: When the spirit tablet was about to return, palace attendants requested that it descend from its seat and be placed on the carriage, with guard of honor and escort as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇太子隨，仍朝夕奠。

translations.literal: The crown prince followed, still offering morning and evening libations.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince followed along, still offering libations morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 至京，先於城外置幄次，列儀衛，鼓吹備而不作。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the capital, first a tent pavilion was set outside the city walls, guard of honor arrayed; drums and pipes prepared but not played.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the capital, a tent pavilion was first set up outside the city walls, the guard of honor was arrayed, and drums and pipes were prepared but not sounded.

sentences.zh: 百官衰服候城外，主入幄次，百官序列，五拜三叩首。

translations.literal: All officials in full mourning waited outside the city; when the tablet entered the pavilion, officials lined up and performed five bows and three kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: All officials in full mourning waited outside the city; when the tablet entered the pavilion, the officials lined up and performed five bows and three kowtows.

sentences.zh: 神主行，百官從。

translations.literal: When the spirit tablet proceeded, all officials followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the spirit tablet set out, all officials followed.

sentences.zh: 至午門外，皇帝衰服迎於午門內，舉哀，步導主升几筵殿。

translations.literal: At the Meridian Gate exterior, the emperor in full mourning welcomed inside the Meridian Gate, raised lamentation, and on foot escorted the tablet to ascend to the spirit table hall.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Meridian Gate, the emperor in full mourning welcomed the tablet inside the gate, raised lamentation, and on foot escorted it up to the spirit table hall.

sentences.zh: 皇帝立殿上，內侍請神主降輿升座，行安神禮。

translations.literal: The emperor stood in the hall; palace attendants requested the spirit tablet descend from the carriage and ascend the seat; the rite of settling the spirit was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stood in the hall; palace attendants requested that the spirit tablet be lowered from the carriage and installed on its seat, and the rite of settling the spirit was performed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝四拜，興，奠酒，讀祝。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed four times, rose, offered wine, and read the prayer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed four times, rose, offered wine, and read the prayer of invocation.

sentences.zh: 俯伏，興，四拜，舉哀。

translations.literal: He prostrated himself, rose, bowed four times, and raised lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself, rose, bowed four times, and lamented.

sentences.zh: 皇太子以下陪拜。

translations.literal: From the crown prince down, all accompanied in bowing.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and all below him accompanied him in bowing.

sentences.zh: 百官于思善門外行禮如儀。

translations.literal: All officials performed rites outside the Gate of Reflecting on Goodness as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: All officials performed the rites outside the Gate of Reflecting on Goodness as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 明日，百官行奉慰禮。

translations.literal: The next day, all officials performed the rite of offering condolences.
translations.idiomatic: The following day, all officials performed the rite of offering condolences.

sentences.zh: 卒哭用虞祭後剛日，禮同虞祭，自是罷朝夕奠。

translations.literal: End of wailing was held on a yang day after the comforting sacrifices; the rites were the same as the comforting sacrifices; from this morning and evening libations ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The end of wailing was observed on a yang day after the comforting sacrifices, with rites identical to those sacrifices; from that point morning and evening libations ceased.

sentences.zh: 祔饗用卒哭之明日，太常寺設醴饌於太廟，如時饗儀，樂設而不作。

translations.literal: Enshrinement offering was held the day after the end of wailing; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set out ceremonial food at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, as in the seasonal feasting rites, with music set out but not played.
translations.idiomatic: The enshrinement offering was held the day after the end of wailing; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices prepared ceremonial food at the Imperial Ancestral Temple according to the seasonal feasting rites, with music set out but not performed.

sentences.zh: 設儀衛傘扇於午門外，內侍進御輦於几筵殿前，皇帝衰服四拜，舉哀。

translations.literal: Guard of honor, parasols and fans were set outside the Meridian Gate; palace attendants brought the imperial palanquin before the spirit table hall; the emperor in full mourning bowed four times and raised lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: The guard of honor, parasols, and fans were arrayed outside the Meridian Gate; palace attendants brought the imperial palanquin before the spirit table hall; the emperor in full mourning bowed four times and raised lamentation.

sentences.zh: 興，哀止，立於拜位之東，西向。

translations.literal: He rose, lamentation ceased; he stood east of the bowing position, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: He rose, his lamentation ceased, and he stood east of the bowing position, facing west.

sentences.zh: 內侍請神主降座升輦，詣太廟祔饗。

translations.literal: Palace attendants requested the spirit tablet descend from the seat and ascend the palanquin, proceeding to the Imperial Ancestral Temple for the enshrinement offering.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants requested that the spirit tablet descend from its seat and be placed on the palanquin, then proceed to the Imperial Ancestral Temple for the enshrinement offering.

sentences.zh: 至思善門外，皇帝易祭服，升輅，隨至午門外，詣御輦前跪。

translations.literal: At the Gate of Reflecting on Goodness exterior, the emperor changed to sacrificial dress, mounted the carriage, followed to outside the Meridian Gate, and proceeded to kneel before the imperial palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Gate of Reflecting on Goodness, the emperor changed into sacrificial dress, mounted his carriage, followed to outside the Meridian Gate, and knelt before the imperial palanquin.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏請神主降輦，皇帝俯伏，興，捧主由左門入，至丹陛上。

translations.literal: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices announced a request that the spirit tablet descend from the palanquin; the emperor prostrated himself, rose, bore the tablet and entered by the left gate, reaching the red steps.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices announced a request that the spirit tablet be lowered from the palanquin; the emperor prostrated himself, rose, bore the tablet, and entered through the left gate to the red steps.

sentences.zh: 典儀唱「太宗文皇帝謁廟」。

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies called out: "Taizong, Cultured Emperor, pays visit to the temple."
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies called out: "Taizong, the Cultured Emperor, pays visit to the temple."

sentences.zh: 至廟前，內侍捧主至褥位，皇帝於後行八拜禮。

translations.literal: Upon reaching before the temple, palace attendants bore the tablet to the cushion position; the emperor behind performed the eight-bow rite.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the temple, palace attendants bore the tablet to the cushion; the emperor followed behind and performed the eight-bow rite.

sentences.zh: 每廟俱同。

translations.literal: Each shrine was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The same procedure was followed at each shrine.

sentences.zh: 內侍捧主北向，太常卿立壇東，西向。

translations.literal: Palace attendants bore the tablet facing north; the Minister of Imperial Sacrifices stood east of the altar, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants bore the tablet facing north, while the Minister of Imperial Sacrifices stood east of the altar, facing west.

sentences.zh: 唱「賜坐」，皇帝搢圭，奉神主安於座，詣拜位行祭禮，如時饗儀。

translations.literal: They called "Bestow the seat"; the emperor inserted the tablet scepter, reverently placed the spirit tablet on the seat, proceeded to the bowing position and performed sacrificial rites as in the seasonal feasting ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: At the call of "Bestow the seat," the emperor inserted the tablet scepter, reverently installed the spirit tablet on its seat, then proceeded to the bowing position and performed the sacrificial rites as in the seasonal feasting ceremony.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏請神主還几筵，皇帝捧主由廟左門出，安奉於御輦。

translations.literal: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices announced a request that the spirit tablet return to the spirit table; the emperor bore the tablet out through the temple's left gate and reverently placed it on the imperial palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices announced a request that the spirit tablet return to the spirit table; the emperor bore it out through the temple's left gate and reverently placed it on the imperial palanquin.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升輅隨，至思善門降輅，易衰服，隨至几筵殿前。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted the carriage and followed; at the Gate of Reflecting on Goodness he descended, changed to full mourning, and followed to before the spirit table hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mounted his carriage and followed; at the Gate of Reflecting on Goodness he dismounted, changed back into full mourning, and followed to before the spirit table hall.

sentences.zh: 內侍請神主降輦，升座。

translations.literal: Palace attendants requested the spirit tablet descend from the palanquin and ascend the seat.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants requested that the spirit tablet be lowered from the palanquin and installed on its seat.

sentences.zh: 皇帝由殿左門入，行安神禮畢，釋服還宮。

translations.literal: The emperor entered by the hall's left gate; when the rite of settling the spirit was complete, he removed mourning dress and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered through the hall's left gate; when the rite of settling the spirit was complete, he removed his mourning dress and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 明日，百官素服行奉慰禮。

translations.literal: The next day, all officials in plain dress performed the rite of offering condolences.
translations.idiomatic: The following day, all officials in plain dress performed the rite of offering condolences.

sentences.zh: 大祥，奉安神主於太廟，禮詳廟制。

translations.literal: At the great expiration, the spirit tablet was reverently settled in the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the rites are detailed in the temple regulations.
translations.idiomatic: At the great expiration, the spirit tablet was reverently installed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the rites are detailed in the temple regulations.

sentences.zh: 皇帝祭告几筵殿，皇太后、皇后以下各祭一罈，王府遣官共祭一罈，在京文武官祭一罈。

translations.literal: The emperor made sacrificial announcement at the spirit table hall; the empress dowager, empress, and all below each offered one jar; the princely establishments dispatched officials to jointly offer one jar; civil and military officials in the capital offered one jar.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made a sacrificial announcement at the spirit table hall; the empress dowager, the empress, and all below each offered one jar; the princely establishments dispatched officials to offer one jar jointly; and civil and military officials in the capital offered one jar.

sentences.zh: 自神主出几筵殿，內侍即撤几筵、帷幄，焚于思善門外。

translations.literal: From when the spirit tablet left the spirit table hall, palace attendants immediately removed the spirit table and curtains and burned them outside the Gate of Reflecting on Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the spirit tablet left the spirit table hall, palace attendants removed the spirit table and curtains and burned them outside the Gate of Reflecting on Goodness.

sentences.zh: 禫祭，遣親王詣陵行禮。

translations.literal: At the removal of mourning sacrifice, imperial princes were dispatched to the tomb to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the removal-of-mourning sacrifice, imperial princes were dispatched to the tomb to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，仁宗崩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi, Emperor Renzong passed away.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongxi, Emperor Renzong died.

sentences.zh: 皇太子還自南京，至良鄉，宮中始發喪，宣遺詔。

translations.literal: The crown prince returned from Nanjing; when he reached Liangxiang, mourning was first announced in the palace and the final testament was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was returning from Nanjing; when he reached Liangxiang, mourning was first announced in the palace and the final testament was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 文武官常服於午門外四拜。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials in regular dress bowed four times outside the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials, wearing regular dress, bowed four times outside the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 宣畢，舉哀，復四拜。

translations.literal: When the proclamation was complete, they raised lamentation and again bowed four times.
translations.idiomatic: When the proclamation was finished, they raised lamentation and bowed four times again.

sentences.zh: 易素服，迎皇太子於盧溝橋，橋南設幕次香案。

translations.literal: They changed to plain dress and welcomed the crown prince at Lugou Bridge; south of the bridge a tent pavilion and incense table were set up.
translations.idiomatic: They changed into plain dress and went to welcome the crown prince at Lugou Bridge; south of the bridge a tent pavilion and incense table were set up.

sentences.zh: 皇太子至，常服，詣次四拜。

translations.literal: When the crown prince arrived, in regular dress he proceeded to the pavilion and bowed four times.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince arrived, still in regular dress, he proceeded to the pavilion and bowed four times.

sentences.zh: 聽宣遺詔，復四拜，哭盡哀。

translations.literal: He heard the final testament proclaimed, again bowed four times, and wept to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: He heard the final testament proclaimed, bowed four times again, and wept to exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 易素服至長安右門下馬，步哭至宮門外，釋冠服，披髮詣梓宮前，五拜三叩首，哭盡哀。

translations.literal: He changed to plain dress; at Chang'an Right Gate he dismounted, walked weeping to outside the palace gate, removed cap and dress, let his hair hang loose and proceeded before the catalpa coffin, five bows and three kowtows, weeping to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: He changed into plain dress; at Chang'an Right Gate he dismounted and walked weeping to outside the palace gate, removed his cap and dress, let his hair hang loose, and proceeded before the imperial bier, where he performed five bows and three kowtows and wept to exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 宮中自皇后以下皆披髮哭。

translations.literal: Within the palace, from the empress down, all let their hair hang loose and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace, from the empress down, everyone let their hair hang loose and wept.

sentences.zh: 皇太子就喪次東，見母后。

translations.literal: The crown prince took his place east of the mourning pavilion and met the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince took his place to the east of the mourning pavilion and met the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 親王以次見皇太子畢，各居喪次，行祭告禮。

translations.literal: Imperial princes in order, after meeting the crown prince, each took their mourning place and performed the announcement sacrifice rite.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes, in order of rank, after meeting the crown prince, each took their place in the mourning pavilion and performed the announcement sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 喪儀俱如舊。

translations.literal: Mourning rites were all as before.
translations.idiomatic: The mourning rites were otherwise unchanged.

sentences.zh: 惟改在京朝夕哭臨三日，後又朝臨止七日，在外止朝夕哭臨三日，無朝臨禮。

translations.literal: Only it was changed that in the capital morning-and-evening weeping and attendance lasted three days; afterward morning attendance ceased at seven days; outside the capital only morning-and-evening weeping and attendance for three days, with no morning attendance rite.
translations.idiomatic: Only this was changed: in the capital, morning-and-evening weeping and attendance lasted three days, and morning attendance then continued for seven days; outside the capital, morning-and-evening weeping and attendance lasted only three days, with no morning attendance rite.

sentences.zh: 文武官一品至四品命婦入哭臨。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials and titled ladies of the first through fourth ranks entered to weep and attend.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials and titled ladies of the first through fourth ranks entered to weep and attend the lying-in-state.

sentences.zh: 服除，禮臣請帝服淺淡色衣、烏紗翼善冠、黑角帶，於奉天門視事。

translations.literal: When mourning was ended, rites officials requested the emperor wear light-colored garments, black gauze Yishan cap, and black horn belt, and conduct affairs at the Gate of Receiving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, rites officials requested that the emperor wear light-colored garments, a black gauze Yishan cap, and a black horn belt, and conduct affairs at the Gate of Receiving Heaven.

sentences.zh: 百官皆淺淡色衣、烏紗帽、黑角帶，朝參如常儀。

translations.literal: All officials wore light-colored garments, black gauze caps, and black horn belts, attending court as in the regular rites.
translations.idiomatic: All officials wore light-colored garments, black gauze caps, and black horn belts, and attended court according to the usual rites.

sentences.zh: 退朝，仍終太宗服制。

translations.literal: After retiring from court, he still completed Taizong's mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: After retiring from court, he still observed the remainder of Taizong's mourning period.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕心何能忍，雖加一日愈於已。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How can my heart bear it — though even one day more is better than ending now."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "How can my heart bear this — even one day more is better than ending it now."

sentences.zh: 」仍素服坐西角門，不鳴鐘鼓，令百日後再議。

translations.literal: He still sat in plain dress at the West Corner Gate, bells and drums were not sounded, and he ordered the matter to be reconsidered after one hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to sit in plain dress at the West Corner Gate, bells and drums were not sounded, and he ordered the matter to be reconsidered after one hundred days.

sentences.zh: 已百日，禮臣復請御奉天門。

translations.literal: When one hundred days had passed, rites officials again requested he mount the throne at the Gate of Receiving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When the hundred days had passed, rites officials again requested that he conduct affairs at the Gate of Receiving Heaven.

sentences.zh: 帝命候山陵事畢。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered them to wait until the mountain tomb affairs were complete.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered them to wait until the mountain tomb affairs were finished.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔營獻陵，帝召尚書蹇義、夏原吉諭曰：「國家以四海之富葬親，豈惜勞費。

translations.literal: Previously, an edict ordered construction of Xianling tomb; the emperor summoned Ministers Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji and instructed them: "The state possesses the wealth of the four seas to bury a parent — how could it begrudge labor and expense."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, an edict had ordered the construction of Xianling; the emperor summoned the ministers Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji and instructed them: "The state possesses the wealth of all under Heaven to bury a parent — how could it begrudge labor and expense."

sentences.zh: 然古聖帝明王皆從儉制。

translations.literal: Yet ancient sage emperors and enlightened kings all followed frugal regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sage emperors and enlightened kings of antiquity all followed frugal regulations.

sentences.zh: 孝子思保其親體魄於永久，亦不欲厚葬。

translations.literal: A filial son who wishes to preserve his parent's body and spirit forever also does not desire lavish burial.
translations.idiomatic: A filial son who wishes to preserve his parent's body and spirit forever does not desire lavish burial either.

sentences.zh: 況皇考遺詔，天下所共知，宜遵先志。

translations.literal: Moreover, the late emperor's final testament is known to all under Heaven — we should follow his prior intent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the late emperor's final testament is known to all under Heaven; we should follow his prior intent.

sentences.zh: 」於是建寢殿五楹，左右廡神廚各五楹，門樓三楹。

translations.literal: Thereupon a sleeping hall of five bays was built, left and right wings and spirit kitchens each of five bays, and a gate tower of three bays.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon a sleeping hall of five bays was built, with left and right wings and spirit kitchens of five bays each, and a gate tower of three bays.

sentences.zh: 其制較長陵遠殺，皆帝所規畫也。

translations.literal: Its scale was far reduced compared with Changling — all was planned by the emperor himself.
translations.idiomatic: Its scale was far reduced compared with Changling, and all of it was planned by the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書蹇義等請祔廟後，素服御西角門視事。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Jian Yi and others requested that after enshrinement at the temple, the emperor in plain dress conduct affairs at the West Corner Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Jian Yi and others requested that after enshrinement at the temple, the emperor conduct affairs in plain dress at the West Corner Gate.

sentences.zh: 至孟冬歲暮，行時饗禮。

translations.literal: When midwinter and year's end arrived, the seasonal feasting rites were performed.
translations.idiomatic: When midwinter and the year's end arrived, the seasonal feasting rites were performed.

sentences.zh: 鳴鐘鼓，黃袍御奉天門視朝。

translations.literal: Bells and drums were sounded; in yellow robe he mounted the throne at the Gate of Receiving Heaven to hold court.
translations.idiomatic: Bells and drums were sounded, and in yellow robe he held court at the Gate of Receiving Heaven.

sentences.zh: 禫祭後，始釋素服。

translations.literal: After the removal of mourning sacrifice, he first removed plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the removal-of-mourning sacrifice did he first doff plain dress.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 宣宗崩，喪葬如獻陵故事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong passed away, funeral and burial followed the Xianling precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong died, the funeral and burial followed the Xianling precedent.

sentences.zh: 惟改命婦哭臨，自三品以上。

translations.literal: Only it was changed that titled ladies attending to weep began from the third rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: Only this was changed: titled ladies attending to weep were limited to those of the third rank and above.

sentences.zh: 英宗崩，遺命東宮過百日成婚，不得以宮妃殉葬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong passed away, his final command was that the heir apparent marry after one hundred days and that palace consorts must not be buried alive in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong died, his final command was that the heir apparent should marry after one hundred days and that palace consorts must not be buried alive in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，百日御奉天門視朝，禮儀悉用吉典。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chenghua acceded, at one hundred days he mounted the Gate of Receiving Heaven to hold court; all ritual followed auspicious regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chenghua acceded, at one hundred days he held court at the Gate of Receiving Heaven, with all ritual following auspicious regulations.

sentences.zh: 憲宗崩，孝宗既除服，仍素翼善冠、麻衣、腰絰視朝，不鳴鐘鼓，百官素服朝參，百日後如常。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chenghua passed away, Emperor Hongzhi, though mourning had ended, still held court wearing plain Yishan cap, hemp garments, and waist mourning bands; bells and drums were not sounded; all officials attended court in plain dress; after one hundred days affairs returned to normal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chenghua died, Emperor Hongzhi, though his mourning period had ended, still held court wearing a plain Yishan cap, hemp garments, and waist mourning bands; bells and drums were not sounded; all officials attended court in plain dress; after one hundred days affairs returned to normal.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年正旦，時未及小祥，帝黃袍御殿受朝。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the first year of Hongzhi, the time not yet having reached lesser expiration, the emperor in yellow robe mounted the hall to receive court.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the first year of Hongzhi, before the lesser expiration had arrived, the emperor in yellow robe mounted the hall to receive the court.

sentences.zh: 次日，仍黑翼善冠，淺淡服、犀帶。

translations.literal: The next day, he again wore black Yishan cap, light-colored dress, and rhinoceros-horn belt.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he again wore a black Yishan cap, light-colored dress, and a rhinoceros-horn belt.

sentences.zh: 及大祥，神主奉安太廟及奉先殿。

translations.literal: When the great expiration came, the spirit tablet was reverently installed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Hall of Venerating the Forebears.
translations.idiomatic: When the great expiration arrived, the spirit tablet was reverently installed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Hall of Venerating the Forebears.

sentences.zh: 至禫祭，免朝。

translations.literal: At the removal of mourning sacrifice, court was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: At the removal-of-mourning sacrifice, court attendance was waived.

sentences.zh: 擇日遣官詣陵致祭。

translations.literal: On a selected day officials were dispatched to the tomb to perform sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On a chosen day officials were dispatched to the tomb to perform sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 孝宗崩，工部言：「大行遺詔，惓惓以節用愛民爲本。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hongzhi passed away, the Ministry of Works reported: "The late emperor's final testament earnestly took frugality and cherishing the people as its foundation."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hongzhi died, the Ministry of Works reported: "The late emperor's final testament earnestly made frugality and cherishing the people its foundation."

sentences.zh: 乞敕內府諸司，凡葬儀冥器並山陵殿宇，務從減省。

translations.literal: We beg an edict to the inner palace offices that all funeral rites, grave goods, and tomb hall buildings be reduced as much as possible.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that an edict be issued to the inner palace offices requiring that all funeral rites, grave goods, and tomb hall buildings be reduced as much as possible.

sentences.zh: 」禮部言：「百日例應變服，但梓宮未入山陵，請仍素翼善冠、麻布袍服、腰絰，御西角門視事，不鳴鐘鼓，百官仍素服朝參。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites reported: "At one hundred days one should normally change dress, but since the catalpa coffin has not yet entered the mountain tomb, we request that he still wear plain Yishan cap, hemp robe, and waist mourning bands, conduct affairs at the West Corner Gate, bells and drums not be sounded, and all officials still attend court in plain dress."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites reported: "At one hundred days dress should normally be changed, but since the imperial bier has not yet entered the mountain tomb, we request that he still wear a plain Yishan cap, hemp robe, and waist mourning bands, conduct affairs at the West Corner Gate without sounding bells and drums, and that all officials continue to attend court in plain dress."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 自辭靈至虞祔，榮王俱在陪列。

translations.literal: From the farewell to the spirit through the comforting sacrifice and enshrinement, the Prince of Rong was always in the accompanying ranks.
translations.idiomatic: From the farewell to the spirit through the comforting sacrifice and enshrinement, the Prince of Rong was always present in the accompanying ranks.

sentences.zh: 既而王以疾奏免。

translations.literal: Afterward the prince memorialized exemption on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Later the prince memorialized asking to be excused on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 禮部請以駙馬等官捧帛朝祖，帝曰：「朝祖捧帛，朕自行。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites requested that imperial sons-in-law and other officials bear the silks at the ancestral visit; the emperor said: "For the ancestral visit and bearing silks, I shall go myself."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites asked that imperial sons-in-law and other officials bear the silks at the ancestral visit; the emperor said: "For the ancestral visit and bearing the silks, I shall go myself."

sentences.zh: 」發引，親王止送至大明門外。

translations.literal: " When the procession departed, imperial princes escorted only to outside the Great Bright Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral procession departed, imperial princes escorted the bier only as far as outside the Great Bright Gate.

sentences.zh: 其在途及至陵臨奠，俱護喪官行禮。

translations.literal: Whether en route or at the tomb for libation attendance, all rites were performed by mourning-guard officials.
translations.idiomatic: Whether along the route or at the tomb for libations, all rites were performed by officials assigned to guard the mourning.

sentences.zh: 後遂爲例。

translations.literal: Later this became the precedent.
translations.idiomatic: This later became the established precedent.

sentences.zh: 世宗崩，令旨免命婦哭臨。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong passed away, a directive exempted ladies of rank from weeping at the lying-in-state.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong died, a directive exempted ladies of rank from weeping at the lying-in-state.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年正月，未及二十七日，帝衰服御宣治門，百官素服、腰絰奉慰。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Longqing, before twenty-seven days had passed, the emperor in full mourning conducted affairs at the Gate of Proclaiming Governance; all officials in plain dress and waist mourning bands presented comforting condolences.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Longqing, before the twenty-seven days had passed, the emperor in full mourning conducted affairs at the Gate of Proclaiming Governance while officials in plain dress and waist mourning bands presented comforting condolences.

sentences.zh: 發引，帝行遣奠禮。

translations.literal: When the procession departed, the emperor performed the dispatch offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral procession departed, the emperor performed the dispatch offering rite.

sentences.zh: 至朝祖，則遣官捧帛行禮。

translations.literal: At the ancestral visit, officials were dispatched to bear the silks and perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: For the ancestral visit, officials were dispatched to bear the silks and perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 梓宮至順天府，皇親命婦及三品以上命婦祭，餘如舊制。

translations.literal: When the catalpa coffin reached Shuntian Prefecture, imperial relatives among ladies of rank and ladies of rank of the third grade and above offered sacrifice; the rest followed the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial bier reached Shuntian Prefecture, imperial relatives among ladies of rank and ladies of rank of the third grade and above offered sacrifice; everything else followed the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，禮部言：「喪服列代皆有制度，而斷自孝宗。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, the Ministry of Rites reported: "Mourning dress for each generation all has regulations, but they take Hongzhi as the cutoff."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, the Ministry of Rites reported: "Each generation has its own regulations for mourning dress, but the standard was set by Hongzhi."

sentences.zh: 蓋孝宗篤於親，喪禮詳且備，故武、世、穆三廟皆宗之。

translations.literal: This is because Hongzhi was devoted to his parents, and his mourning rites were detailed and complete; therefore the three temples of Wuzong, Shizong, and Muzong all took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi was deeply devoted to his parents, and his mourning rites were detailed and complete; for this reason the reigns of Wuzong, Shizong, and Muzong all took him as their model.

sentences.zh: 今遵舊制，以衰服御文華門視事，百官素服朝參，候梓宮發引除。

translations.literal: Now we follow the old regulations: in full mourning conduct affairs at the Wenhua Gate, all officials in plain dress attend court, and wait until the catalpa coffin procession departs before doffing mourning.
translations.idiomatic: We now follow the old regulations: conduct affairs at the Wenhua Gate in full mourning, with all officials attending court in plain dress, and doff mourning only after the imperial bier procession has departed.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 明自仁宗獻陵以後，規制儉約。

translations.literal: From the Ming, after Renzong's Xianling tomb, the regulations were economical.
translations.idiomatic: From the Hongxi Emperor's Xianling tomb onward, Ming regulations were economical.

sentences.zh: 世宗葬永陵，其制始侈。

translations.literal: When Shizong was buried at Yongling, its regulations first became extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong was buried at Yongling, tomb regulations first became extravagant.

sentences.zh: 及神宗葬定陵，給事中惠世揚、御史薛貞巡視陵工，費至八百餘萬云。

translations.literal: When Shenzong was buried at Dingling, Supervising Secretary Hui Shiyang and Censor Xue Zhen inspected the tomb works; the expense is said to have reached more than eight million.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong was buried at Dingling, Supervising Secretary Hui Shiyang and Censor Xue Zhen inspected the tomb construction; the cost is said to have exceeded eight million taels.
